title: Ananda Temple, Bagan
summary: The Ananda Temple in Bagan (Pagan), Myanmar, is an early 12th-century Buddhist temple built under King Kyanzittha of the Pagan dynasty around 1105 CE. Regarded as an architectural masterpiece transitional between Mon and Burmese temple traditions, it is laid out on a symmetrical Greek-cross plan with four massive standing Buddhas facing the cardinal directions around a solid masonry core.

uncertainty.note: Built during the reign of King Kyanzittha (reigned c. 1084-1112/13 CE); Northern Illinois University's SEAsite dates the temple to c. 1105 AD (with 1112 AD also cited), while the Government of India Press Information Bureau notes construction in the early 12th century. Restored following the 1975 and 2016 earthquakes; standing today.
